message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (Texas Property Code, Chapter 24) and related statutes: | Category | Key Rights | Practical Implications | |----------|------------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep records of the deposit amount and any receipts. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a livable condition (plumbing, heating, structural integrity, etc.).
• Must keep the property free of pests and comply with health & safety codes. | • Report problems promptly; keep written records. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withholding** | • If landlord fails to repair a major defect, tenant may pay the repair cost and deduct it from rent, or withhold rent until repairs are made. | • Document the defect and give written notice to landlord. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenancy.
• For eviction: 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease violation, 60‑day notice for lease termination. | • Written notices are required; keep copies. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenant has the right to live without unreasonable interference from landlord or other tenants. | • Landlord cannot enter without proper notice (usually 24 hours). | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlord must provide reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of entries. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • Fair Housing Act applies. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions (e.g., banning pets unless justified). | • Review lease carefully; negotiate terms. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must comply with lease terms and give proper notice. | • Check lease for rent‑increase clauses. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the legal process: serve notice, file complaint, court hearing, and obtain judgment. | • Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Security Deposit Deductions** | • Landlord may deduct for unpaid rent, damages beyond normal wear, cleaning costs, and other legitimate charges. | • Landlord must provide itemized statement. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • If landlord fails to repair a major defect, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent. | • Must provide written notice and keep receipts. | | **Right to Sublet** | • Tenant may sublet only with landlord’s consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | • Obtain written permission. | | **Right to Dispute** | • Tenants can dispute unlawful deductions or eviction in court. | • Keep documentation. | ### How to Protect Your Rights 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, photos of defects, and a written log of any repairs or complaints. 2. **Know the Notice Periods** – Always check the lease for specific notice requirements; if none, default to the statutory periods above. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipt to establish proof. 4. **Check the Lease** – Verify that the lease complies with Texas law (e.g., security deposit limits, notice periods). 5. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face eviction or disputes, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or local legal aid organization. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code, Chapter 24** – Statutory framework for residential leases. - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Provides consumer guides and forms. - **Legal Aid of North Texas** – Offers free legal assistance for low‑income residents. - **Texas Tenants’ Rights Hotline** – Phone line for immediate advice (check local listings). --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney familiar with Texas landlord‑tenant law.
